description: Canonical chess motif taxonomy — the weakness-category vocabulary the RSI loop targets. Each motif's `detectedBy` names the engine component that currently recognizes it (a fact specialist, the eval, or the search); `detectedBy: null` is a DETECTION GAP = an item on the RSI detector roadmap. `category` is tactical | positional; `family` groups related motifs.
sources: chesstempo.com/tactical-motifs + chesstempo.com/positional-motifs (site returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher; the canonical standard motif set was used for these and should be reconciled against the live pages)

motifs.name: Fork
motifs.definition: One piece attacks two or more targets at once.

motifs.name: Knight Fork
motifs.definition: A knight forks two or more targets.

motifs.name: Pawn Fork
motifs.definition: A pawn attacks two pieces.

motifs.name: Double Attack
motifs.definition: Two threats created in one move (by one or more pieces).

motifs.name: Discovered Attack
motifs.definition: Moving one piece unveils an attack from another.

motifs.name: Discovered Check
motifs.definition: A discovered attack that gives check.

motifs.name: Double Check
motifs.definition: Two pieces check the king simultaneously; the king must move.

motifs.name: Windmill
motifs.definition: A repeating series of forced discovered checks/attacks.

motifs.name: Absolute Pin
motifs.definition: A piece pinned to its king (illegal to move).

motifs.name: Relative Pin
motifs.definition: A piece pinned to a more valuable piece behind it.

motifs.name: Cross Pin
motifs.definition: A piece pinned along two lines at once.

motifs.name: Skewer
motifs.definition: Attack a valuable piece, winning the lesser piece behind it.

motifs.name: X-Ray Attack
motifs.definition: A slider attacks through an enemy piece to a target behind.

motifs.name: X-Ray Defense
motifs.definition: A slider defends a piece through an enemy piece.

motifs.name: Deflection
motifs.definition: Force a defender off its defensive post.

motifs.name: Decoy
motifs.definition: Lure a piece to a bad square.

motifs.name: Attraction
motifs.definition: Draw a piece (often the king) onto a vulnerable square.

motifs.name: Interference
motifs.definition: Interpose to cut the line between two enemy pieces.

motifs.name: Overloading the Defender
motifs.definition: A defender tasked with too many duties is exploited.

motifs.name: Removing the Defender
motifs.definition: Eliminate the piece guarding a key square/target.

motifs.name: Capturing the Defender
motifs.definition: Capture the defender to undermine a target.

motifs.name: Clearance
motifs.definition: Vacate a square or line for another piece.

motifs.name: Interposition / Indirect Defense
motifs.definition: Defend via a counter-threat rather than direct guard.

motifs.name: Battery
motifs.definition: Two pieces aligned on a file/rank/diagonal to multiply force.

motifs.name: Queen + Bishop Battery
motifs.definition: Queen and bishop on the same diagonal.

motifs.name: Two Rooks Battery
motifs.definition: Two rooks doubled on a file/rank.

motifs.name: Alekhine's Gun
motifs.definition: Doubled rooks backed by the queen on a file.

motifs.name: Sacrifice
motifs.definition: Give up material for a larger gain.

motifs.name: Greek Gift Sacrifice
motifs.definition: Bxh7+ sacrifice against the castled king.

motifs.name: Demolition of Pawn Structure
motifs.definition: Sacrifice to strip the king's pawn cover.

motifs.name: Desperado
motifs.definition: An already-lost piece grabs material before dying.

motifs.name: Back-Rank Mate
motifs.definition: Mate on the back rank behind unmoved pawns.

motifs.name: Smothered Mate
motifs.definition: Knight mate with the king boxed in by its own pieces.

motifs.name: f2/f7 Weakness
motifs.definition: Exploit the only-king-defended f2/f7 square.

motifs.name: Prevent Castling
motifs.definition: Keep the enemy king stuck in the center.

motifs.name: Cross-check
motifs.definition: Answer a check with a check.

motifs.name: Mate Threat
motifs.definition: A threatened forced mate constrains the opponent.

motifs.name: Perpetual Check
motifs.definition: Force a draw by endless checks.

motifs.name: Perpetual Attack
motifs.definition: Force a draw by endlessly attacking a key target.

motifs.name: Stalemate Tactics
motifs.definition: Save a lost position via stalemate.

motifs.name: Zwischenzug
motifs.definition: An in-between move (often a check) before the expected recapture.

motifs.name: Tempo Tactics
motifs.definition: Gain time with forcing threats.

motifs.name: Counter Threat
motifs.definition: Meet a threat with a bigger threat.

motifs.name: Quiet Move
motifs.definition: A non-checking, non-capturing move that sets up an unstoppable threat.

motifs.name: Zugzwang
motifs.definition: Any move worsens the opponent's position.

motifs.name: Triangulation
motifs.definition: Lose a tempo with the king to pass the move.

motifs.name: Trapped Piece
motifs.definition: A piece has no safe squares.

motifs.name: Domination
motifs.definition: A piece is lost despite nominally having squares.

motifs.name: Hanging Piece
motifs.definition: An undefended piece can be captured for free.

motifs.name: Counting
motifs.definition: A capture sequence wins material on the exchange count.

motifs.name: Simplification
motifs.definition: Trade into a winning endgame.

motifs.name: Endgame Tactics
motifs.definition: Tactics specific to endgames.

motifs.name: Underpromotion
motifs.definition: Promote to a non-queen to fork/avoid stalemate.

motifs.name: Pawn Breakthrough
motifs.definition: A pawn sacrifice creates an unstoppable passer.

motifs.name: Advanced Passed Pawn
motifs.definition: Use an advanced passer's promotion threat tactically.

motifs.name: Isolated Pawn
motifs.definition: A pawn with no friendly pawns on adjacent files.

motifs.name: Doubled Pawns
motifs.definition: Two friendly pawns on the same file.

motifs.name: Backward Pawn
motifs.definition: A pawn behind its neighbors that can't safely advance.

motifs.name: Passed Pawn
motifs.definition: No enemy pawn can stop it from promoting.

motifs.name: Hanging Pawns
motifs.definition: Two adjacent pawns with no pawn support, both potential targets.

motifs.name: Pawn Islands
motifs.definition: Groups of connected pawns separated by open files.

motifs.name: Pawn Majority
motifs.definition: More pawns than the opponent on one wing.

motifs.name: Minority Attack
motifs.definition: Advance a pawn minority to create weaknesses.

motifs.name: Outpost
motifs.definition: A protected square no enemy pawn can attack, ideal for a knight.

motifs.name: Weak Square
motifs.definition: A square that can't be defended by a pawn.

motifs.name: Color Complex Weakness
motifs.definition: Chronic weakness on one color of squares.

motifs.name: Open File
motifs.definition: A file with no pawns, a highway for rooks.

motifs.name: Half-Open File
motifs.definition: A file with only enemy pawns, pressure for rooks.

motifs.name: Rook on the 7th
motifs.definition: A rook on the 7th rank attacks pawns and confines the king.

motifs.name: Bishop Pair
motifs.definition: Both bishops vs bishop+knight or two knights, strong in open positions.

motifs.name: Bad Bishop
motifs.definition: A bishop blocked by its own fixed pawns.

motifs.name: Good Knight / Outpost Knight
motifs.definition: A knight on a strong, supported, unattackable square.

motifs.name: Piece Activity
motifs.definition: More active, better-placed pieces.

motifs.name: Centralization
motifs.definition: Pieces (esp. king in the endgame) controlling the center.

motifs.name: Space Advantage
motifs.definition: More territory, cramping the opponent.

motifs.name: King Safety
motifs.definition: The relative exposure/shelter of the king.

motifs.name: Blockade
motifs.definition: Plant a piece in front of a passed pawn to stop it.

motifs.name: Prophylaxis
motifs.definition: Prevent the opponent's plan before pursuing your own.

motifs.name: Overprotection
motifs.definition: Defend a key point more than necessary to free the defenders' activity.

motifs.name: Fianchetto
motifs.definition: Develop a bishop to the long diagonal behind a g/b-pawn.
